x: The appearance of Eric Stroud could bring a bit of depth to our long distance side as could Paul Wiltshire to our sprint team. Pat Duncan did manage to put on a set of gear and compete in club races although questions were asked as to who the friend was under his shirt.

John Hall was with the leading pack for the first four miles despite a heavy cold, and he gallantly held on for 7th position with the race being won by K.Emsley of Steyning. Bob Picton was our second man home with Doug Fotheringham and Eric Stroud, in only his second race for the Club, behind him.

Paul Wiltshire put up a distinguished time and to quote one of the judges, "could be very good if he will get his arms right". Doug Fotheringham for the second week led home Eric Stroud, although Eric was walking better than his "Garnet" performance.
Dave McMullen and Ray Hall walked their way back into the county team and Eric Stroud turned in a commendable performance on the tough course.
A heavy downpour took place during the first 4 miles whilst Arthur Thompson led but eventually John Nye came through to win. Eric Stroud turned in another personal best, followed by John Keown.
The tenacity of Dave McMullen, D.Hall and John Dunsford showed this spirit and the pity was that E.Stroud could not be included in the team and rewarded for his fine walk.
Admittedly our line up for the '50' of seven starters included three who had never walked a '50' before - Eric Stroud, John Hall and Martin Yates - but where were the others?

Unfortunately, due mainly to inexperience, Eric Stroud retired at 50 kilos leaving only three to finish. With winner Ladany of Israel under the eight hours, Belgrave's first man was Dave King in 23rd place.

It was an oversight in the last issue of the 'Belgravian' that no mention was made of Johnny Morris, John Keown and Eric Stroud, all of whom competed in the notorious 'Brighton' and hence doubled our number of finishers of the year before.
